title: Failover follow-ups
description: Smaller items from the failover reviews.
acceptanceCriteria: Liveness URL: a worker process started with `--liveness-database-url` connects its liveness lock and its lease keeper through that URL and nothing else: Postgres sees at most two connections from it there (one while it has no job, two while it has one), also after the lock is taken again and the keeper reconnects several times, and every other statement of the process (claims, looks, registration, job rows, hints, scans, sweeps, migrations) goes through `JELLYSCALE_DATABASE_URL`; fails today, where the flag stops the start

Liveness URL: without the flag a worker's lock and keeper connect through `JELLYSCALE_DATABASE_URL` exactly as today, and an `api` or `stream` process given the flag starts and opens no connection to it

Liveness URL: a value that is not a Postgres URL stops the start with an error naming the flag, before anything is written to Postgres; one that parses but refuses connections stops nothing (the worker logs why, claims no job, retries as an unreachable lock connection is retried today, and takes jobs once it connects); one behind a transaction-mode pooler is logged as a lock Postgres does not show is logged today, the line naming `--liveness-database-url`

Liveness URL: with it refusing connections to every worker while the main URL answers (three workers, each with a job, viewers asking for segments), an interruption shorter than a lease less a heartbeat leaves every job its row, worker and ffmpeg and forgets no worker; one longer than a lease ends each job `cancelled`, never `failed`, with no spec refused and no job claimed meanwhile, and the next request starts each again at the first segment not stored

Liveness URL: with `JELLYSCALE_DATABASE_URL` behind a real session-mode pooler (PgBouncer in a container on a Docker-assigned port) and the liveness URL direct, with real processes of every role: a film transcodes and its segments are served, a text subtitle is extracted, a library scan and a sweep run, and a worker killed (SIGKILL) mid-job is replaced before its lease, as it stood at the kill, would have run out (a 30 s lease); the only connections from the workers that bypass the pooler are their liveness ones

Liveness URL: docs/running.md (Configuration and the `max_connections` arithmetic), docs/transcoding.md (Connections) and ARCHITECTURE.md (roles table, control-plane ceiling) name the flag, say the liveness URL must be a direct, session-mode connection, say which pooler modes the main URL may then sit behind (session mode at least) and what breaks under a mode they do not allow, and give what N workers then cost Postgres in direct connections (2N)

One reaper: at every cluster size one worker at a time, the reaper, looks for dead workers: with 60 live workers, as with 3, over at least 20 look periods every statement of a worker that reads `pg_locks` or forgets a node comes from one worker and the other workers send none, so the count does not grow with the number of workers (counted on every connection of every worker); fails today, where each worker sends two such statements a look

One reaper: the reaper killed (SIGKILL, real processes, at least three workers) while it holds a job a viewer waits on: exactly one of the others takes the role, also when several try at once, forgets it on today's conditions (its lock found gone in two looks at least the `confirmGap` apart, the new reaper's own lock held in the same snapshot and not lost within the `hold`), and its job is claimed before its lease, as it stood at the kill, would have run out (a 30 s lease); the same when the reaper and another worker are killed together, both forgotten and both jobs taken over

One reaper: the role does not rest with a worker that cannot do it: while the reaper is stopped (SIGSTOP) with its connections standing, while its looks go unanswered (a database delay past the look's bound), and while its own lock has ended within the `hold`, a worker that holds a trusted lock does the forgetting, so a worker killed meanwhile is forgotten and its job claimed before its lease (30 s) would have run out; the stopped or slow reaper is itself not forgotten and its leases are not cut

One reaper: a worker that is not the reaper still learns in time that it was forgotten: with its lock gone while its connection stands, or forgotten while it could not lock again, it finds its row gone within a `lookPeriod` (at once on the hint) and every transcode ffmpeg of it is gone before a replacement's starts; a worker whose lock ended and whose row is there goes on with its jobs

One reaper: a worker of the release before (its row and its lock as today, taking no part in choosing the reaper, reaping by itself) running beside the new ones is never forgotten while it holds its lock and is forgotten on the same conditions when it is killed, and its own reaping forgets no live new worker

One reaper: nothing else about liveness changes: a worker other than the reaper that is killed is forgotten on today's conditions with its jobs' leases cut to the `forgottenLease`, several at once and no live one; the existing kill, stop, outage, lease-keeper and fault-schedule checks (JS-029, JS-066, JS-104, JS-105) pass with their assertions and bounds untouched; after an outage that ended every connection whichever worker is the reaper forgets nobody within the `hold`; a replica (api, stream) still forgets nobody

One reaper: ARCHITECTURE.md rules 4 and 6, DOMAINS 25 and docs/transcoding.md say there is one reaper, how it is chosen and replaced (killed, stopped, slow, its lock lost), and what reaping then costs Postgres at 50 and at 400 workers, in place of the per-worker figures they give today

Subtitle leases: a worker killed (SIGKILL) while it runs `subtitle_jobs` rows has their leases cut when it is forgotten, as its transcode jobs' are: in the statement that deletes its row, each running row of every kind (a film's text pass, a subtitle file beside the film, a `.sup`, fonts, chapter pictures) is left at most the `forgottenLease` from then and never a longer lease than it had; shown with several rows of one worker beside a transcode job, and with two workers forgotten in one look

Subtitle leases: another worker then claims each such row before the lease it had at the kill would have run out (a 30 s lease, so a build that waits the lease out fails), the request that was waiting is answered with its track and no answer of 500 or more, and the file is read by one more ffmpeg run, not two; fails today, where the row waits out its lease

Subtitle leases: what a lost lease costs a row is unchanged: each takeover counts one attempt, a row whose lease is lost on its third claim fails with today's error and is remembered as today, an ordinary ffmpeg failure still fails the row at once, and a worker stopped gracefully still puts its job back in the queue uncounted

Subtitle leases: none is cut for a worker that is not forgotten: one that only lost its lock and took it again (its row there), every worker through a Postgres outage shorter than a lease less a heartbeat, and a worker stopped (SIGSTOP) with its connections standing each keep their rows' leases and finish with the same ffmpeg; a stopped worker's row is taken over only once the lease it last renewed has run out

Subtitle leases: a worker forgotten while it lives (its lock gone with its connection standing, or unable to lock again) ends the ffmpeg of every extraction and chapter job it runs within the `forgottenLease` and before another worker's ffmpeg for the same row starts, moves no cut lease later (bar the one renewal already waiting on the row when the reap commits, as DOMAINS 25 allows a transcode job) and writes nothing to a row another worker has claimed; the interleaving is forced, not waited for

Subtitle leases: DOMAINS 25 and 43 and docs/transcoding.md (which says today that subtitle extractions and chapter pictures keep their 10 second lease, whoever dies) state the new bound for a killed worker and the fallback that stays (the lease, when no connection closes)

Claim and re-lock: a claim sent before the worker's row is found gone and committed after the worker has stopped its jobs, locked again and put its row back takes a job the worker runs: the job is `running` on this worker with an ffmpeg that stores its first segment (or is still `queued`), never written `cancelled` and never left `running` with no ffmpeg of the worker, the viewer waiting on it is served by that same job row with no second job for the spec; the interleaving is forced by holding the claim's statement, so the check fails on every run of today's tree

Claim and re-lock: the bound of that claim is stated and checked: a claim committed before the worker is forgotten is one of its jobs and ends with them (`cancelled`, never `failed`, started again by the viewer's request), and no claim commits while the worker's row is gone

Claim and re-lock: a claim that overlaps only a re-lock (the lock's connection ended and taken again, the row never gone) costs no job: with the lock's connection ended over and over while jobs are queued and claimed (real contention, at least 200 rounds), every queued job is claimed by one worker and runs, none ends `cancelled`, none has two owners, and a worker still claims nothing while it does not hold its lock

Rollback note: docs/running.md's Rolling update says how to roll back across this release's liveness changes: a worker of the release before stops at start on `--liveness-database-url` and takes its lock and renews its leases through `JELLYSCALE_DATABASE_URL`, so the flag is removed and that URL made a direct, session-mode one again before such a worker starts; and it gives the order workers and replicas roll in, up and back, or says that none is needed

Rollback note: it says what a fleet of both releases does meanwhile: workers of the release before each still look for the dead beside the one reaper, no live worker of either release is forgotten and a dead one of either is, a subtitle row of a worker forgotten by an old worker waits out its lease as before, and a worker from before the liveness lock (a row that took no lock) is never forgotten and is taken over at its lease
